title: S100P mediates IL-13/ATF4-driven epithelial barrier dysfunction in eosinophilic asthma: a potential biomarker and therapeutic target.
authors: Li, Dengke; Yin, Yuan; Hao, Ruizhi; Ren, Yesong; Gu, Shengwei; Wang, Hongyu; Han, Lu; Ye, Sheng; Li, Lingshu; Yao, Xin; Zeng, Xiaoning
one_liner_zh: 该文研究哮喘中S100P介导的IL-13/ATF4上皮屏障功能障碍，虽涉及分子对接与动力学模拟，但核心是疾病机制与生物标志物，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: In allergic asthma, a detrimental cycle of epithelial barrier destruction, driven predominantly by type 2 inflammation, facilitates allergen exposure to deeper tissues. However, the precise mechanisms underlying this process remain poorly understood. METHODS: A bioinformatics analysis was performed using public datasets and an independent cohort of asthma patients. Single-cell profiling further elucidated the role of S100 calcium-binding protein P (S100P) in this condition. To investigate the impact of S100P on barrier integrity, human bronchial epithelial cells (16HBE) were stimulated with interleukin-13 (IL-13). The functional interaction between S100P and potential therapeutic compounds was evaluated by molecular docking and dynamics simulation. RESULTS: Our findings revealed significant alterations in the transcriptional regulation of the S100P, with protein levels correlating closely with lung function and eosinophilic inflammation. S100P was predominantly localized in airway epithelial cells (AECs), particularly in the goblet and club cells. It acts as a pivotal signal in maintaining epithelial barrier integrity by regulating tight junction proteins, such as ZO-1 and occludin, and altering transepithelial electrical resistance. Mechanistically, IL-13 markedly upregulated S100P expression in AECs, likely via activation of transcription factor 4 (ATF4). Molecular docking and dynamics simulations demonstrated that S100P interacts with the clinically established antihistamine astemizole and the immunosuppressant celastrol, both of which protect against S100P-induced barrier disruption. CONCLUSIONS: Our work identified S100P as a key mediator of airway epithelial barrier dysfunction in asthma, shedding light on the crucial signaling of the IL-13/ATF4/S100P axis. These findings highlight the dual potential of S100P as both a biomarker and a therapeutic target, offering promising strategies for barrier protection in clinical asthma management.
abstract_zh: 背景：在过敏性哮喘中，由2型炎症主导驱动的上皮屏障破坏的有害循环，促进过敏原暴露于更深层组织。然而，这一过程背后的精确机制仍知之甚少。方法：利用公共数据集和独立哮喘患者队列进行了生物信息学分析。单细胞分析进一步阐明了S100钙结合蛋白P（S100P）在此病症中的作用。为研究S100P对屏障完整性的影响，用人支气管上皮细胞（16HBE）经白细胞介素-13（IL-13）刺激。通过分子对接和动力学模拟评估了S100P与潜在治疗化合物之间的功能相互作用。结果：我们的发现揭示了S100P转录调控的显著变化，其蛋白水平与肺功能和嗜酸性炎症密切相关。S100P主要定位于气道上皮细胞（AECs），特别是在杯状细胞和棒状细胞中。它通过调节紧密连接蛋白（如ZO-1和occludin）并改变跨上皮电阻，在维持上皮屏障完整性中起关键信号作用。机制上，IL-13显著上调AECs中S100P的表达，可能通过激活转录因子4（ATF4）实现。分子对接和动力学模拟表明，S100P与临床已确立的抗组胺药阿司咪唑和免疫抑制剂雷公藤红素相互作用，两者均能保护免受S100P诱导的屏障破坏。结论：我们的工作将S100P确定为哮喘中气道上皮屏障功能障碍的关键介质，揭示了IL-13/ATF4/S100P轴的关键信号传导。这些发现凸显了S100P作为生物标志物和治疗靶点的双重潜力，为临床哮喘管理中的屏障保护提供了有前景的策略。
